layoutData.tagline: Established Community Pharmacy with Long-Term Care Expertise and Specialty Compounding

layoutData.body:
Beacon Specialty Pharmacy Inc. has served Ottawa and Eastern Ontario for 19 years under the ownership of Dr. Helen Park. Since opening in April 2006, the pharmacy has evolved from a neighbourhood retail operation into a specialized provider combining community dispensing, long-term care pharmacy services, and advanced non-sterile compounding.

The business operates from a 4,850 square foot facility in the Merivale Crossing plaza on Merivale Road, strategically positioned to serve both its community patient base and a portfolio of 14 long-term care and retirement homes representing 1,046 beds across Eastern Ontario. This dual revenue model has driven consistent growth and produced $9,120,400 in revenue in fiscal 2024, a record year for the pharmacy.

Long-term care services form the operational backbone, generating $2,736,100 in 2024. The pharmacy provides comprehensive medication management including automated strip packaging, medication reviews, stat order delivery guaranteed within four hours, and 24/7 on-call pharmacist support. The LTC portfolio is anchored by a master service agreement with Maplecrest Senior Living covering five homes, renewed in September 2024 through August 2027. No LTC home has been lost since 2019, a testament to the quality of service and the deep relationships built by Daniel Okafor, the LTC lead pharmacist with 11 years tenure who personally knows the medication profiles of virtually every resident.

The pharmacy maintains NAPRA Level B non-sterile compounding certification with a documented library of 340 formulas spanning hormone replacement therapies, pain management, pediatric suspensions, and veterinary compounding for six Ottawa-area clinics. The compounding operation, led by Mei-Lin Tran since 2018, passed the Ontario College of Pharmacists focused assessment in March 2024 with only two minor documentation items, both closed within one month. Compounding revenue reached $820,800 in 2024, generated entirely through professional referrals with zero advertising spend.

Community dispensing remains robust at $4,560,200 in 2024, serving an estimated 6,000 to 7,000 active patients in the Merivale area. The patient base includes working families with strong private insurance coverage, balancing the overall payer mix at approximately 55 to 56 percent Ontario Drug Benefit. Professional services contributed $364,900 in 2024, including approximately 2,900 flu vaccinations and roughly 1,100 minor ailment assessments in the first year of Ontario's expanded scope program.

The business benefits from an experienced and stable team. Core personnel include Daniel Okafor (LTC lead, 11 years), Mei-Lin Tran (compounding lead, 7 years), Sophie Lavoie (lead technician, 14 years), Carol Whitfield (billing and accounts receivable manager), and Jordan Clarke (packaging operations, 9 years). The 23-person team operates without union representation and receives market-competitive compensation, benefits, and RRSP matching.

Beacon Specialty Pharmacy holds all required licences and accreditations. The Ontario College of Pharmacists certificate of accreditation is current and in good standing, with a clean assessment history. The pharmacy participates in mandatory incident reporting and maintains a joint health and safety committee.

The business is positioned at an inflection point. Packaging automation is running at approximately 60 percent capacity and can absorb 300 to 400 additional beds without capital investment. A back storage area has been evaluated for conversion to NAPRA Level C hazardous compounding capability, which would unlock additional high-margin referrals currently sent elsewhere. With strong fundamentals, diversified revenue streams, multi-year contracts, embedded expertise, and clear expansion pathways, Beacon Specialty Pharmacy represents a rare opportunity to acquire a profitable, operationally mature pharmacy business with significant upside for a strategic buyer.

left.content:
Beacon's long-term care pharmacy services are built on clinical excellence, operational reliability, and deep institutional relationships that have been cultivated over more than a decade.

The pharmacy provides comprehensive medication management to all 14 homes, centered on automated strip packaging using two leased PackRight machines. Each resident's medications are organized into time-specific pouches labeled with name, date, time, and medication details, reducing administration errors and streamlining care staff workflow. The packaging operation is managed by Jordan Clarke, with final clinical verification by Daniel Okafor for virtually all long-term care orders.

Stat order delivery is guaranteed within four hours and typically completed in two hours. Two dedicated delivery drivers operate west and south routes using delivery vans equipped for temperature-sensitive medications. A rear loading door installed during the 2019 facility relocation enables efficient staging and dispatch. The pharmacy maintains 24/7 on-call pharmacist service for urgent clinical questions, medication clarifications, and after-hours stat orders.

Eleven of the 14 homes are connected via CareMAR eMAR interface, providing real-time integration between the pharmacy dispensing system and each facility's electronic medication administration records. This integration reduces transcription errors and accelerates communication of medication changes.

The long-term care operation is led by Daniel Okafor, who joined the pharmacy in March 2014 and has served as the primary pharmacist contact for all homes for 11 years. Daniel personally knows the medication profiles of virtually every resident across the portfolio and maintains direct relationships with administrators and directors of care at each facility. His tenure and institutional knowledge are central to contract retention and service quality. As administrators and directors of care move between facilities across the Eastern Ontario long-term care network, they bring their trusted pharmacy relationships with them.

This combination of clinical expertise, operational infrastructure, and deep personal relationships has resulted in zero long-term care home losses since 2019.

left.title: Capabilities & Certification
left.content:
Beacon Specialty Pharmacy maintains NAPRA Level B non-sterile compounding certification, a specialized capability that differentiates the pharmacy in the Ottawa market and drives strong referral relationships across both human and veterinary medicine.

The compounding operation is led by Mei-Lin Tran, who joined in 2018 and has built a documented, compliant practice with 340 master formulation records maintained to NAPRA template standards. Mei-Lin personally rebuilt all formulation documentation and spearheaded the pharmacy's successful Ontario College of Pharmacists focused compounding assessment in March 2024, which resulted in Level B compliance certification with only two minor action items—updates to 12 veterinary formulas to the new template format, completed within one month.

The compounding room was purpose-built during the pharmacy's 2019 relocation, with upgrades in 2023 including a containment ventilated enclosure to meet evolving NAPRA standards. All compounding operations follow rigorous quality controls, ingredient verification protocols, and beyond-use dating procedures reviewed and approved by the Ontario College of Pharmacists.

The practice serves three distinct specialties: veterinary compounding for 6 clinics across Ottawa (transdermal gels for cats, flavoured suspensions for dogs, custom-dosed preparations), bioidentical hormone replacement therapy creams and troches for Ottawa prescribers, and custom pain management formulations including ketamine, gabapentin and combination creams referred by dermatologists and pain clinics, plus pediatric suspensions in child-friendly flavours and strengths unavailable commercially.

All compounding business is referral-driven through prescriber relationships held by Mei-Lin, with zero advertising spend. The veterinary compounding network has grown purely through word-of-mouth among veterinarians who trust the quality and consistency of formulations for companion animals.

left.title: Regulatory Standing & Assessment History
left.content:
Beacon Specialty Pharmacy Inc. holds Ontario College of Pharmacists certificate of accreditation CA-30-5518, covering community pharmacy operations including non-sterile compounding and long-term care and retirement home services. The pharmacy has been continuously accredited since 2006 with no discipline findings against the pharmacy or its designated manager.

The College conducts routine and focused assessments to verify compliance with standards of practice. Assessment history reflects consistent acceptable performance: October 8, 2019 routine assessment (acceptable, no action items); November 16, 2021 routine assessment (acceptable, 1 recommendation implemented December 2021); May 24, 2023 routine assessment (acceptable with follow-up, 3 items remediated and closed July 10, 2023); and March 12, 2024 focused assessment for non-sterile compounding (Level B compliant, 2 action items closed April 30, 2024). The next routine assessment is expected in 2026.

The March 2024 compounding assessment confirmed NAPRA Level B compliance for the pharmacy's non-sterile compounding operations. The two minor action items identified were updates to 12 veterinary master formulation records to align with the current NAPRA template format and completion of annual personnel competency re-assessment documentation. Both items were closed within six weeks.

In July 2023, the pharmacy identified a controlled substance loss of approximately 1,840 tablets (high-strength controlled-release oxycodone and hydromorphone) with an estimated value of $7,900, stolen over approximately five months by one pharmacy technician. The employee was terminated immediately upon discovery. The pharmacy reported the loss to Health Canada within 10 days (July 14, 2023), filed a police occurrence report with Ottawa Police Service, and notified the Ontario College of Pharmacists. No charges were laid. Enhanced controls were implemented immediately: perpetual narcotic inventory with weekly counts, dual sign-off requirements on all narcotic receipts, and camera surveillance over the narcotic safe. No narcotic discrepancies have been identified since August 2023.

The pharmacy participates in the Ontario College of Pharmacists' mandatory anonymous medication incident reporting program. Incident rates reaching patients have declined steadily: 7 incidents in 2022, 5 in 2023, and 4 in 2024. None resulted in patient harm requiring hospitalization. Quarterly continuous quality improvement meetings are held to review incidents and implement process controls.

Beacon Specialty Pharmacy maintains a strong compliance record with a demonstrated commitment to continuous quality improvement and transparent incident management.

Medication incidents reaching patients have declined steadily over the three-year period: 7 incidents in 2022, 5 in 2023, and 4 in 2024. None of these incidents resulted in patient harm requiring hospitalization. The pharmacy participates in the Ontario College of Pharmacists' mandatory anonymous medication incident reporting program and conducts quarterly continuous quality improvement meetings to review trends and implement preventive measures.

In July 2023, the pharmacy experienced a controlled substance loss totaling approximately $7,900 due to employee theft. A pharmacy technician had stolen 1,840 tablets of high-strength controlled-release oxycodone and hydromorphone over approximately five months. Upon discovery, the employee was immediately terminated. The pharmacy reported the loss to Health Canada on July 14, 2023, filed a police occurrence report with Ottawa police within 10 days, and notified the Ontario College of Pharmacists as required.

In response to the incident, the pharmacy implemented enhanced narcotic control procedures that have proven effective. Weekly perpetual narcotic counts are now conducted with dual signatures required on all narcotic receipts. A security camera was installed directly over the narcotic safe. Sophie Lavoie, the lead technician with 14 years' tenure, now personally manages all weekly narcotic counts. There have been no narcotic discrepancies of any kind since August 2023.

In 2024, the pharmacy received an Ontario Drug Benefit post-payment verification recovery notice for approximately $6,200 related to insufficient documentation for certain claims. The pharmacy immediately remediated the documentation practices identified in the audit, and no ongoing billing restrictions were imposed.

The pharmacy's OCP assessment history reflects consistent acceptable performance: routine assessments in October 2019, November 2021, and May 2023 all resulted in acceptable ratings. The May 2023 assessment included three action items that were remediated and formally closed on July 10, 2023. The March 2024 focused assessment of non-sterile compounding operations resulted in Level B compliance certification with two action items (updating 12 veterinary formulas to the new NAPRA template format), both closed by April 30, 2024.

There have been no disciplinary findings against the pharmacy or its designated manager in the Ontario College of Pharmacists' public register. The pharmacy has had no lost-time WSIB claims from 2022 through 2024 and maintains a joint health and safety committee as required.

Beacon Specialty Pharmacy operates in Ottawa's competitive retail pharmacy market from its Merivale Crossing plaza location at 1742 Merivale Road. The competitive landscape shifted in October 2023 when a large-format chain pharmacy opened approximately one kilometre away, on the other side of the Hunt Club intersection. The new competitor operates with extended hours until midnight and carries a broad front-store assortment.

This entry negatively impacted Beacon's over-the-counter product sales, contributing to a repositioning of the front store away from general retail toward pharmacist-fitted compression stockings, mobility aids, and home health care products where clinical expertise provides a defensible edge. Despite the proximity and hours advantage of the chain competitor, Beacon's prescription volume remained stable throughout 2024. The pharmacy's relationship-based service model—where staff know patients by name and provide personalized counselling—has proven resilient.

Beacon's long-term care business operates in a relationship-driven referral environment that is largely insulated from traditional retail competition. The pharmacy's LTC portfolio was built over more than a decade through personal referrals and care director transitions across the Eastern Ontario long-term care network. As administrators and directors of care move between facilities, they bring their trusted pharmacy partners with them. Daniel Okafor, the LTC lead pharmacist with eleven years' tenure, personally knows every resident medication list and maintains direct relationships with care staff at all 14 homes. This depth of institutional knowledge and trust is difficult for competitors to replicate.

The compounding side of the business is entirely referral-based and has never been advertised. Mei-Lin Tran, the compounding lead since 2018, has built a network of prescriber relationships with Ottawa dermatologists, hormone therapy specialists, pediatric prescribers, and six veterinary clinics. The 340 documented formulas—all maintained to NAPRA template standards—and the pharmacy's NAPRA Level B compliance create a technical barrier to entry. Veterinary compounding in particular relies on word-of-mouth among veterinarians who trust the quality and consistency of transdermal gels and flavoured suspensions for companion animals.

The Ontario pharmacy market is shaped by provincial drug benefit policies and generic pricing regulations that apply uniformly to all pharmacies. Beacon's Ontario Drug Benefit revenue—representing approximately 55 to 56 percent of total dispensing revenue and stable at that level for several years—is subject to the same reimbursement terms as every other ODB provider. Competition on government-funded prescriptions is therefore won on service, accessibility, and clinical value rather than price.

Beacon benefits from an exclusive pharmacy clause in its plaza lease that prevents the landlord from renting to another pharmacy in Merivale Crossing, providing territorial protection within its immediate trade area. Combined with the pharmacy's deep operational expertise in long-term care services, specialized compounding capabilities meeting national accreditation standards, and a tenured team that holds the key relationships in both the LTC network and the compounding referral base, Beacon has built competitive positioning that is difficult for generalist competitors to match.

layoutData.body:
Dr. Helen Park is retiring after 19 years of ownership and is offering Beacon Specialty Pharmacy for sale to facilitate a planned succession.

The decision to sell is driven by personal retirement planning. Dr. Park has built the pharmacy from a neighbourhood retail operation into a specialized provider of long-term care services and advanced compounding, and now seeks to transition the business to a buyer who can continue that growth trajectory and retain the exceptional team in place.

The transition plan is structured to ensure continuity for patients, long-term care home partners, and staff. Dr. Park will remain as the pharmacy's designated manager until the buyer's pharmacist is approved by the Ontario College of Pharmacists, a process that typically takes three to six months. Following that initial period, Dr. Park will continue working three days per week for up to one year after closing, providing hands-on training and operational support.

A key component of the transition is the personal introduction to every long-term care home relationship. Dr. Park will accompany the new owner to all 14 homes and introduce them personally to administrators and directors of care, ensuring a smooth handoff of these critical institutional relationships that represent 30.0% of total revenue.

The seller is committed to a successful transition and will provide comprehensive training across all aspects of the business: long-term care contract management and home relationships, compounding operations and prescriber relationships, community patient care and clinical services, staff management and scheduling, supplier relationships and inventory management, regulatory compliance and College reporting, and billing systems including ODB, private adjudication, and retirement home accounts.

This level of transition support—anchored by up to 18 months of direct involvement—provides the buyer with continuity, knowledge transfer, and relationship preservation that are essential to maintaining the pharmacy's strong performance and reputation.
